title: Classify PR commits by content in pr_commits, with evidence write-up
summary: Retry of rejected job 20261024-161559-rxjg: rewrite pr_commits in athena-core land.rs to classify commits in remote_base..head by content (records_only, declared_intervention, job_landing via the gate's closing_jobs), with no trailers. The earlier code was right; it failed only for a missing change description. Audience: Sri and the verifier.

defaults_applied.how: Criteria name tests that run the classification and refusal behavior.
Criteria require core and CLI tests to pass, with clippy and fmt clean.
The fix reuses closing_jobs and removes the trailer rule, rather than patching the one failing fixture.
Criteria name the commands the verifier can run.
The change description and docs are written for an outside reader.
One focused change; the evidence-check idea is excluded.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The request means redoing the same job with the same accepted reading and corrections, and fixing what the verifier found.

A grep found pr_commits called only from gh.rs GitLandingRecords::commits. reconcile.rs and the CLI reconcile tests reach it through GitLandingRecords. run.rs retry_landing and drain.rs PrLander do not call it, so they stay unchanged unless a real dependency turns up. I did not verify this myself here.
The change description is a docs deliverable: a section of the CHANGELOG entry, or a doc comment, that lists every caller and writer, the test covering each, and the commands actually run.
The CLI test fixture duplication is minor. Sharing it needs a non-cfg(test) helper, which is optional; if duplicated, a comment may note the drift risk.
The pre-handover evidence check proposed by the introspection is out of scope. This request is only to retry the job.

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. A realistic-range test (reading, dispatch and introspection commits, an owner-path commit under a directory with a nested .gitattributes '* athena-exclude', an intervention adding records/interventions/<month>/<id>.json, then a job's candidate, verification and outcome; no Athena-Job trailers) yields records_only x4, declared_intervention, and job_landing carrying that job and its verification id.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. Blocked-then-landed: a commit adding candidate, verification and a blocked outcome is records_only. A later commit adding only outcome-landed.json plus governed work is job_landing for that job, reusing the gate's closing_jobs.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core land::`. Refusal tests each make pr_commits return an error naming the commit sha: governed change that is neither intervention nor closing records; landing with no verification; landing whose outcome exists but is not landed (a real blocked outcome, not a missing one); owner-path commit without the exclusion.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core` and `cargo test -p athena-cli --test reconcile`. All pass, including the 5 core reconcile tests and the 2 CLI reconcile tests that failed before. Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh::` to check that landing commits carry kind, job and verification from pr_commits and pass LandingCommit::validate.

pr_commits and PrCommit no longer read trailers or mention Athena-Job. Doc comments state the content rules and that closing_jobs is the single source of truth. The old trailer-count tests are removed. An empty range is still an error.

The change description (in the CHANGELOG entry) lists every caller of pr_commits and every writer of landing records: gh.rs GitLandingRecords::commits, reconcile.rs via GitLandingRecords, run.rs retry_landing, and drain.rs PrLander. Each has the test that covers it, or the reason it needed no change, and the commands actually run.
docs/design/records-history.md and CHANGELOG.md describe content-based classification and no longer describe the trailer rule.
Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean.

out_of_scope: Building the pre-handover evidence check in Athena proposed by the introspection.
Changing the semantics of the gate's closing_jobs beyond exposing it for reuse.
departures: Cost and time are above the reference because this is a multi-crate change with core and CLI test runs. Pass probability is slightly higher than the reference because the cause of the earlier failure is known.
